title: Man shot by Ont. police may have link to Pickton
article: The 38-year-old man fatally shot by police in an Oakville, Ont., park over the weekend died of multiple gunshot wounds, autopsy results revealed Monday.

But authorities in Ontario and British Columbia could not confirm whether the dead man, Steve Remian, was the same person whose name surfaced at the Robert (Willie) Pickton trial -- where a jury is now deliberating on the fate of the Port Coquitlam pig farmer in the slayings of six of the women who went missing from Vancouver's notorious Downtown East Side.

DNA belonging to a Steve Remian was discovered on a blanket along with that of Pickton and one of the victims. The name Steve J. Remian was also found on the label of a suitcase in Pickton's workshop. The evidence was mentioned at the year-long trial -- though Remian was not a suspect.
The man who was shot by police in southeast Oakville at 2:33 a.m. Saturday was driving a vehicle with B.C. plates and was reported to have recently returned from the West Coast.
Neither the Special Investigations Unit now probing the Oakville shooting nor the RCMP's Missing Women's Joint Task Force in B.C. would confirm they were the same Steve Remian.
